items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: they had us both in the band together, you know, playing in a jazz band.

ctx.x: And I just wondered how long he'd known you and all that.

Oh, Willie, Willie would have been known before I was born. Willie's, he was my oldest brother. How old is your oldest brother? My oldest brother, he's beautiful, Willie Parker, he's around his 80s or something odd. He's my oldest brother. Then I had two brothers of size, you understand, he was older than me.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: That's a man I've seen for many years. But I knew he's a wonderful musician.

ctx.x: Now, that man? Mm-hmm. We want his house. Oh! Many times I'm going to York, he got to go to his house. He lived, good off, um, that big square he lived off. Where is he parked? Yeah, that's right. He lived there. And the last time I was in New York, he come and got me, him and his wife, okay? It was me and George and Kid Howard. And man, what them people put on the table, then he had plenty of company drivers, you know? But Dad, they're supposed to eat and drink, man. That's a pretty story I see. Really, really,…

Well, he got an older boy too. I know, Peppa. Peppa. He's off. He's off. He was off in college. Oh, he was off in college, yeah. See, I wanted to ask you about Willie Foster. We were talking about him earlier, sales and on.

Who was that for us? The bass player. Oh, you mean the violin player? Man, listen, I'm going to be fit with you. That's a man I've seen for many years. But I knew he's a wonderful musician. He is a wonderful musician, tell me. But I ain't seen Bill for as long as Bill. I'm in for as long as Bill. He's really a good musician. Yeah.
